challenges.title: Official Languages of Afghanistan
challenges.context: As a language researcher, you need to list all official languages spoken in Afghanistan. The data is spread across two tables: countries (country information) and languages (language details per country).

instructions.description: Start by selecting the country_code from the countries table where the country_name is 'Afghanistan'.
instructions.hint: Use SELECT code FROM countries WHERE country_name = 'Afghanistan'.

instructions.description: Inner join the languages table with the countries table on the country code. Use the alias 'c' for countries and 'l' for languages.
instructions.hint: INNER JOIN languages l ON c.code = l.code

instructions.description: Filter the result to only show official languages (official = true). Select the country_name and language name.

challenges.starter_code:
-- Tables available: countries, languages
-- Write your query below
challenges.solution_code:
SELECT c.country_name, l.name
FROM countries c
INNER JOIN languages l ON c.code = l.code
WHERE c.code = 'AFG' AND l.official = true;
challenges.output_description: Two rows showing the official languages of Afghanistan: Dari and Pashto.
hints: You need to combine both tables on the country code column.
Look for the official column in the languages table to filter.
challenges.learning_outcome: Student demonstrates ability to perform an INNER JOIN between two tables and filter results.

challenges.title: Countries Without Currency Data
challenges.context: A financial analyst wants to identify all countries that have no currency information in the database. This might indicate missing data.

instructions.description: Perform a LEFT JOIN between countries (c) and currencies (cur) on the country code.
instructions.hint: LEFT JOIN currencies cur ON c.code = cur.code

instructions.description: Filter the joined result to find rows where the currencies table has no entry (i.e., the join column from currencies is NULL).
Select only the country_name from countries to list the countries without currency data.

challenges.starter_code:
-- Tables: countries, currencies
-- Write a query to find countries missing currency info.
challenges.solution_code:
SELECT c.country_name
FROM countries c
LEFT JOIN currencies cur ON c.code = cur.code
WHERE cur.code IS NULL;
challenges.output_description: List of countries that do not have a matching row in the currencies table. In the sample data, Netherlands (NLD) is missing.
hints: Remember that a LEFT JOIN keeps all rows from the left table; unmatched rows from the right table have NULLs.
Use IS NULL on a column that comes from the right table to find missing rows.
challenges.learning_outcome: Student learns to use LEFT JOIN with IS NULL to implement an anti‑join pattern and identify missing relationships.

challenges.title: Countries with Economic Data in 2015 or 2019
challenges.context: You need a unified list of all country codes that appear in either the 2015 or the 2019 economic dataset, without duplicates.

instructions.description: Select the distinct country code from the 2015 economic data.
Select the distinct country code from the 2019 economic data.
Combine the two result sets using UNION to remove duplicates.

challenges.starter_code:
-- Tables: economies2015, economies2019
-- Write a query that returns distinct country codes present in either table.
challenges.output_description: Distinct country codes present in either dataset. Sample includes AFG (2015), AGO and ALB (2019).
hints: Both queries must return the same number of columns (here just one).
challenges.learning_outcome: Student demonstrates the use of UNION to combine two result sets and eliminate duplicates.

challenges.title: Continent with Highest Average GDP per Capita in 2015
challenges.context: Management wants to identify which continent had the highest average GDP per capita in 2015 to focus investment. You'll need to compute the average per continent using a subquery in the FROM clause.

instructions.description: Write a subquery that joins countries and economies2015 on code, groups by continent, and calculates the average gdp_percapita. Alias the subquery as 'continent_avg'.
instructions.hint: FROM (SELECT c.continent, AVG(e.gdp_percapita) AS avg_gdp FROM countries c INNER JOIN economies2015 e ON c.code = e.code GROUP BY c.continent) AS continent_avg

instructions.description: In the outer query, select continent and the average (rounded to two decimal places) from the subquery.
Order the result by the average descending and limit to 1 to get the continent with the highest average.

challenges.starter_code:
-- Tables: countries, economies2015
-- Write a query that finds the continent with the highest average GDP per capita in 2015.
challenges.solution_code:
SELECT continent, ROUND(avg_gdp, 2) AS avg_gdp
FROM (
    SELECT c.continent, AVG(e.gdp_percapita) AS avg_gdp
    FROM countries c
    INNER JOIN economies2015 e ON c.code = e.code
    GROUP BY c.continent
) AS continent_avg
ORDER BY avg_gdp DESC
LIMIT 1;
challenges.output_description: The continent with the highest average GDP per capita and the rounded average value. In the sample data, only Asia has 2015 data, so it appears as the top.
hints: You need a derived table (subquery in FROM) to compute the averages per continent.
The outer query should sort and limit to pick the top continent.
challenges.learning_outcome: Student proves ability to use a subquery in the FROM clause, aliased, and perform aggregation and sorting outside it.

challenges.title: Countries with Both Currency and 2015 Economic Data
challenges.context: An integration check requires finding all countries that have both currency information and 2015 economic data in the database. You'll need to chain two inner joins across three tables.

instructions.description: Start with the countries table (alias c). Inner join it with the currencies table (cur) on the country code.
instructions.hint: INNER JOIN currencies cur ON c.code = cur.code

instructions.description: Chain another inner join with the economies2015 table (e) on the same country code.
instructions.hint: INNER JOIN economies2015 e ON c.code = e.code

instructions.description: Select the country name from countries. The result will contain only countries that exist in all three tables.

challenges.starter_code:
-- Tables: countries, currencies, economies2015
-- Write a query that returns country names that appear in all three tables.
challenges.solution_code:
SELECT c.country_name
FROM countries c
INNER JOIN currencies cur ON c.code = cur.code
INNER JOIN economies2015 e ON c.code = e.code;
challenges.output_description: List of country names that have records in all three tables. Sample data shows Afghanistan (AFG) in all three.
hints: Chain INNER JOINs: the ON clause of the second join refers to a column from the first table.
Each join filters out rows that don't match, so only countries present in all tables survive.
challenges.learning_outcome: Student demonstrates chaining multiple INNER JOINs to combine data from three related tables.
